name: glb-designer-showcase
description: Asset Studio Iteration 7 Stage 11b — showcase integration build. Scripts a COMPLETE catalog-quality chesterfield-style sofa end-to-end in ONE session, exercising as many Asset Studio systems as compose naturally, then proves the whole thing round-trips and lands in the real flat. Phases: (1) insert the Sofa frame TEMPLATE with tuned ergonomic sliders; (2) MATERIALS — rich velvet (KHR sheen) on the cushions + oiled-wood clearcoat legs + plump; (3) PRECISION — face-snap the two seat cushions flush (magnet abut via the __glbDesignerPrecision.drag seam); (4) DIAMOND TUFTING + stitch lines on both seat cushions via the real inspector UI (Stage 7c/10c); (5) PIPING welts traced round each seat-cushion top-face perimeter (Stage 5); (6) preview under Studio rig vs Room IBL (Stage 8a) — the same pose, lighting-only difference; (7) SAVE through the optimize-on-save path (Stage 6f) and assert the persisted assetSpec envelope embeds every system; (8) RESTORE the saved def's editable parts (Stage 0) and assert part/group/decal counts survive the persistence round-trip on a REAL complex asset; (9) close the designer and PLACE the saved sofa in the flat's Living/Dining room at HIGH quality — the money shot. Run with SHOT_GPU=1 (velvet sheen + Room IBL + High tier read truthfully only on a real GPU). This scenario doubles as the Stage-11b integration regression test.

steps.name: assert-template-parts
steps.comment: The Sofa frame flattened into a 'Sofa frame' PartGroup: 4 lathe legs, a base box, a back box, 2 arm boxes, and 2 seat + 2 back velvet cushions (velvet = sheen>0). Assert the structural parts + exactly 4 velvet cushions landed.
steps.eval: (function(){ const s=window.__glbDesigner.getSpec(); const g=(s.partGroups||[]).find(x=>x.name==='Sofa frame'); if(!g) throw new Error('Sofa frame group missing'); const legs=s.parts.filter(p=>p.kind==='lathe'); if(legs.length!==4) throw new Error('expected 4 lathe legs, got '+legs.length); const cushions=s.parts.filter(p=>p.kind==='box' && (p.sheen??0)>0); if(cushions.length!==4) throw new Error('expected 4 velvet cushions, got '+cushions.length); const seats=cushions.filter(p=>p.size[2]>0.3); if(seats.length!==2) throw new Error('expected 2 seat cushions (deep Z), got '+seats.length); console.log('11B_TEMPLATE parts='+s.parts.length+' legs='+legs.length+' cushions='+cushions.length); })()

steps.name: apply-materials
steps.comment: PHASE 2 — MATERIALS. Deterministic setSpec seam (the stage10c/stage8a precedent — material-UI walking is fragile headless): (a) ALL upholstered fabric parts (the template tags them with the grey #8a8f98 FABRIC look) get a rich oxblood colour #5b2733 + a strong sheen (KHR_materials_sheen) + a warm sheen tint — the cushions AND the arms/backrest frame, so the whole piece reads as one consistent velvet (an earlier pass that keyed only on the velvet sheen preset left the arms grey — fixed here); the cushions (which carry the velvet preset's sheen) additionally get plump 0.7 (crowned upholstery, the tuft/wrinkle prerequisite) and are renamed 'Seat cushion N' / 'Back cushion N' so the layer rows + tuft/piping UI are addressable; (b) the 4 tapered legs get an oiled-wood look — warm walnut colour + a clearcoat layer (KHR_materials_clearcoat) with a soft roughness, the physical field that reads as a hand-rubbed oil finish. The dark-wood base plinth is left as wood.
steps.eval: (function(){ const api=window.__glbDesigner; const s=JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(api.getSpec())); let seatN=0, backN=0; s.parts=s.parts.map(p=>{ if(p.kind==='lathe'){ return { ...p, color:'#4f3a26', roughness:0.5, metalness:0, clearcoat:0.4, clearcoatRoughness:0.55 }; } if(p.kind==='box' && p.color==='#8a8f98'){ const isCushion=(p.sheen??0)>0; const base={ ...p, color:'#5b2733', sheen:1, sheenColor:'#8a4a56', sheenRoughness:0.55, roughness:0.82, metalness:0 }; if(isCushion){ const isSeat=p.size[2]>0.3; return { ...base, name:(isSeat?('Seat cushion '+(seatN++)):('Back cushion '+(backN++))), plump:0.7 }; } return { ...base, name:'Upholstered frame' }; } return p; }); api.setSpec(s); })()

steps.name: assert-materials

steps.eval: (function(){ const s=window.__glbDesigner.getSpec(); const legs=s.parts.filter(p=>p.kind==='lathe'); if(!legs.every(p=>(p.clearcoat??0)>0)) throw new Error('legs missing clearcoat (oiled-wood physical field)'); const seats=s.parts.filter(p=>/^Seat cushion/.test(p.name||'')); if(seats.length!==2) throw new Error('expected 2 named seat cushions, got '+seats.length); if(!seats.every(p=>p.color==='#5b2733' && (p.sheen??0)>0 && (p.plump??0)>0.5)) throw new Error('seat cushions missing rich colour / sheen / plump'); console.log('11B_MATERIALS legsClearcoat='+legs[0].clearcoat+' seatPlump='+seats[0].plump); })()

steps.name: precision-abut-seats
steps.comment: PHASE 3 — PRECISION. The template lays the two seat cushions with a reveal gap; tighten them into a seamless bench line via the __glbDesignerPrecision.drag seam. NOTE (integration finding): face-to-face MAGNETIC snapping (Stage 6d) is documented as unavailable on a grouped MEMBER — and template cushions are members of the 'Sofa frame' group — so the drag commits the value verbatim (no auto-snap). We therefore compute the exact abut target from the live geometry (cushion 1's -X face meets cushion 0's +X face) and drive the gizmo to it, achieving a precise flush placement numerically. Record the pre-drag reveal gap to prove it closed.
steps.eval: (function(){ const s=window.__glbDesigner.getSpec(); const seats=s.parts.filter(p=>/^Seat cushion/.test(p.name||'')).sort((a,b)=>a.position[0]-b.position[0]); if(seats.length!==2) throw new Error('need 2 seat cushions'); const c0=seats[0], c1=seats[1]; const c0maxX=c0.position[0]+c0.size[0]/2; const preGap=(c1.position[0]-c1.size[0]/2)-c0maxX; const targetX=c0maxX+c1.size[0]/2; window.__abut={ c0id:c0.id, c1id:c1.id, preGap }; window.__glbDesignerPrecision.drag(c1.id, [targetX, c1.position[1], c1.position[2]]); })()

steps.name: assert-abut-flush
steps.comment: Seat cushion 1's -X face now meets seat cushion 0's +X face flush (gap ~0), closing the template's reveal gap.
steps.eval: (function(){ const s=window.__glbDesigner.getSpec(); const c0=s.parts.find(p=>p.id===window.__abut.c0id); const c1=s.parts.find(p=>p.id===window.__abut.c1id); const c0maxX=c0.position[0]+c0.size[0]/2; const c1minX=c1.position[0]-c1.size[0]/2; const gap=c1minX-c0maxX; if(Math.abs(gap)>1e-3) throw new Error('seat cushions not flush — gap '+gap); if(!(window.__abut.preGap>Math.abs(gap))) throw new Error('reveal gap did not close (pre '+window.__abut.preGap+' post '+gap+')'); console.log('11B_PRECISION preGap='+window.__abut.preGap+' postGap='+gap); })()

steps.name: assert-tufting
steps.comment: Both seat cushions carry a DIAMOND tuft grid with stitches on, and tagged button + stitch decals were generated (an offset lattice with diagonal stitch lines running the dimple valleys — the chesterfield read).
steps.eval: (function(){ const s=window.__glbDesigner.getSpec(); const seats=s.parts.filter(p=>/^Seat cushion/.test(p.name||'')); if(seats.length!==2) throw new Error('need 2 seat cushions'); for(const c of seats){ if(!c.tuft) throw new Error(c.name+' has no tuft grid'); if(c.tuft.pattern!=='diamond') throw new Error(c.name+' not diamond: '+c.tuft.pattern); if(c.tuft.stitches!==true) throw new Error(c.name+' stitches off'); const dec=(s.decals||[]).filter(d=>d.tuft && d.partId===c.id); const buttons=dec.filter(d=>d.kind==='button'); const lines=dec.filter(d=>d.kind==='stitch'); if(buttons.length!==c.tuft.rows*c.tuft.cols) throw new Error(c.name+' button count '+buttons.length+' != '+(c.tuft.rows*c.tuft.cols)); if(lines.length===0) throw new Error(c.name+' has no stitch decals'); } const totalTuft=(s.decals||[]).filter(d=>d.tuft).length; window.__tuftTotal=totalTuft; console.log('11B_TUFTING totalTuftDecals='+totalTuft); })()

steps.name: assert-saved
steps.comment: End-to-end save proof: a new UserGltfDef named 'Showcase Chesterfield' whose assetSpec envelope embeds the plumped oxblood seat cushions, the diamond tuft grids + stitch decals, the piping welts, and the oiled-wood clearcoat legs. Version asserted loosely (>=11) so a concurrent envelope bump can't false-fail.

waitFor.store: state.userFurniture.length > window.__glbBaseline && state.userFurniture.some(d => d.name === 'Showcase Chesterfield' && typeof d.assetSpec === 'string' && (() => { try { const env = JSON.parse(d.assetSpec); if (env.kind !== 'asset' || typeof env.v !== 'number' || env.v < 11) return false; const s = env.payload; const seats = s.parts.filter(p => /^Seat cushion/.test(p.name||'')); if (seats.length !== 2) return false; if (!seats.every(p => (p.plump||0)>0 && p.tuft && p.tuft.pattern==='diamond' && p.tuft.stitches===true && p.color==='#5b2733')) return false; const welts = s.parts.filter(p => p.kind==='sweep' && Array.isArray(p.sweepPoints)); if (welts.length !== 2) return false; const legs = s.parts.filter(p => p.kind==='lathe'); if (!legs.every(p => (p.clearcoat||0)>0)) return false; const tuftDecals = (s.decals||[]).filter(x => x.tuft); return tuftDecals.length > 0; } catch { return false } })())

steps.name: capture-saved-def
steps.comment: The Save-asset flow AUTO-CLOSES the designer on success. Capture the saved def id + envelope counts from the store before reopening.
steps.eval: (function(){ const d=window.__store.getState().userFurniture.find(x=>x.name==='Showcase Chesterfield'); window.__savedId=d.id; const env=JSON.parse(d.assetSpec); window.__savedCounts={ parts:env.payload.parts.length, groups:(env.payload.partGroups||[]).length, decals:(env.payload.decals||[]).length }; console.log('11B_SAVED id='+d.id+' parts='+window.__savedCounts.parts+' groups='+window.__savedCounts.groups+' decals='+window.__savedCounts.decals); })()

steps.name: assert-restore-counts
steps.comment: The restored spec's part / group / decal counts EXACTLY match what was saved — a REAL complex asset (velvet cushions, diamond tuft + stitch decals, piping welts, oiled legs) survived the persistence round-trip with nothing dropped.
steps.eval: (function(){ const s=window.__glbDesigner.getSpec(); const now={ parts:s.parts.length, groups:(s.partGroups||[]).length, decals:(s.decals||[]).length }; const exp=window.__savedCounts; if(now.parts!==exp.parts) throw new Error('part count drift: restored '+now.parts+' vs saved '+exp.parts); if(now.groups!==exp.groups) throw new Error('group count drift: restored '+now.groups+' vs saved '+exp.groups); if(now.decals!==exp.decals) throw new Error('decal count drift: restored '+now.decals+' vs saved '+exp.decals); const seats=s.parts.filter(p=>/^Seat cushion/.test(p.name||'')); if(!seats.every(p=>p.tuft&&p.tuft.pattern==='diamond')) throw new Error('restored seat cushions lost their diamond tuft'); console.log('11B_RESTORE parts='+now.parts+' groups='+now.groups+' decals='+now.decals+' (matches saved)'); })()

steps.failMessage: the saved chesterfield was not placed in the Living/Dining room

steps.name: deselect
steps.comment: Deselect the just-placed item so the inspector panel closes and the money shot shows the unobstructed scene.

steps.name: zoom-in-1
steps.comment: Pull the room-editor camera in toward the room (wheel-only camera moves stay inside the scene; an orbit-drag as the FIRST move can swing past the room into empty space, so zoom first).

steps.name: orbit-hero
steps.comment: Now tilt to a top-3/4 angle looking down into the room (reads the tufted seat clearly).

steps.name: zoom-in-2
steps.comment: Zoom the rest of the way for the hero framing.

steps.name: shot-money
steps.comment: THE MONEY SHOT — the custom-built oxblood diamond-tufted chesterfield sofa placed in the real 4-room HDB Living/Dining room, rendered at High quality under daylight. The whole Asset Studio pipeline (template -> materials -> precision -> tufting -> piping -> save -> place) end-to-end in one scene, alongside the flat's existing furniture.

steps.name: wheel-in
steps.comment: Zoom further for a detail read (velvet sheen + diamond tufting + oiled legs in the real scene).

steps.name: shot-money-detail
steps.comment: THE MONEY SHOT (detail) — a closer look at the placed chesterfield in the flat.
